title: VaultKey — Almost Two Factors
objective: Sign in with the correct password but skip the one-time code step. Reach the account page anyway.

verifier.condition: The protected account page is served to a session whose server-side record shows the one-time code step was never completed.

weakness: The protected page checks only whether a session exists, not whether that session's multi-step login actually reached the completed state, so a session minted after the password step alone is already enough.
vulnerableEndpoint: GET /account (checks session presence, not its mfaVerified flag)
seededData: User alice with a known password and a 6-digit one-time code you are never shown (correct verification is possible but not required for the exploit). In-memory.

credentials.label: User account
credentials.note: After signing in you'll be asked for a 6-digit code you don't have.

hints: Watch what happens the moment you submit the correct password, before you ever touch the code field. Are you already holding something?
The one-time-code page and the account page are two different requests. What does the server actually check on each?
Try going straight to the page you'd land on after a full, successful sign-in.
burpNotes: Submit the password step in Repeater and inspect the Set-Cookie header, then send that cookie straight to /account without ever visiting /verify-code.
